evals.prompt: Is V-Sync currently on?
evals.expected_output: The current V-Sync state, read back from the machine. The agent should answer with a read-only query and change nothing.
assertions: Read g-assist-mcp-skill/SKILL.md
Listed the available tools before calling one
Called gassist_query_feature_status with the vsync feature
Reported the state without changing it
Did not call gassist_set_display_vsync

evals.prompt: Turn off V-Sync.
evals.expected_output: gassist_set_display_vsync is destructive and confirmation-gated, so the host asks the user to approve and the change is applied only on approval. The agent should relay the outcome from the result text.
assertions: Read g-assist-mcp-skill/SKILL.md
Called gassist_set_display_vsync with enable "0" (a string, not a boolean)
Let the host collect the user's confirmation rather than supplying one
Did not include a confirm argument in the tool call
Reported the outcome based on the text of the result

evals.prompt: Change my display resolution to 1920x1080.
evals.expected_output: The resolution change is confirmed once before it is applied and once after, because it auto-reverts in about 20 seconds unless kept. Both prompts are expected and the tool is called once.
assertions: Read g-assist-mcp-skill/SKILL.md
Took the resolution value from the live tool schema rather than a remembered list
Called gassist_set_display_res exactly once
Warned the user the screen may flicker and a second keep-or-revert prompt will follow
Treated the second prompt as the expected keep-or-revert question, not an error
Did not call the tool again to finish or retry the change
Reported accurately whether the new mode was kept or reverted

evals.prompt: Set my refresh rate to 500 Hz.
evals.expected_output: No consumer panel supports 500 Hz, so either the value is absent from the live enum or the call comes back with prose saying it could not be done. Either way the agent must report failure, not success.
assertions: Read g-assist-mcp-skill/SKILL.md
Checked the live refresh rate enum for the requested value
Read the text of the result rather than relying on the isError flag
Reported that the refresh rate was not changed
Offered the highest rate the panel actually supports
Did not report success because the call returned without an error

evals.prompt: Set this PC up for competitive shooters.
evals.expected_output: A short sequence: read the current V-Sync and G-SYNC state, turn V-Sync off, and raise the refresh rate to the panel's maximum. The agent should explain the gated changes before triggering the prompts.
assertions: Read g-assist-mcp-skill/SKILL.md
Read current state with gassist_query_feature_status before changing anything
Used three or fewer tool calls
Told the user which changes need confirmation before triggering the prompts
Took the refresh rate value from the live enum
Summarised what is now true based on the result text

evals.prompt: What has my GPU temperature and utilisation been doing over the last two minutes?
evals.expected_output: A read-only metrics plot over the requested window. The agent should request GPU temperature and GPU utilisation for two minutes.
assertions: Read g-assist-mcp-skill/SKILL.md
Called gassist_graphdata with GPU_TEMP and GPU_UTIL
Set time to 2 and unit to mins
Changed no settings

evals.prompt: Set my external monitor's colour temperature to 6500K.
evals.expected_output: gassist_set_display_color_temp accepts a fixed Kelvin enum that includes 6500, and is available only when the display supports it. If the tool is present the agent should call it with kelvin 6500; if it is gated off on this display it should say so rather than invent a tool.
assertions: Read g-assist-mcp-skill/SKILL.md
Checked that gassist_set_display_color_temp is present in the available tools
Called it with kelvin 6500 taken from the tool's enum, or reported it is unavailable on this display
Did not invent a tool name or a non-enum Kelvin value

evals.prompt: Cap my frame rate at 120 FPS.
evals.expected_output: A frame-rate limit set with the frame-rate limiter tool. The agent should select gassist_frl with fps 120 and must not change the refresh rate instead.
assertions: Read g-assist-mcp-skill/SKILL.md
Listed the available tools before calling one
Called gassist_frl with fps 120
Did not change the refresh rate instead

evals.prompt: Turn on G-SYNC.
evals.expected_output: gassist_set_display_gsync enables G-SYNC and is confirmation-gated, so the host collects approval. The agent should call it with enable "1" (a string) and relay the outcome, without adding a confirm argument.
assertions: Read g-assist-mcp-skill/SKILL.md
Called gassist_set_display_gsync with enable "1" (a string, not a boolean)
Let the host collect the user's confirmation rather than supplying one
Did not enable G-SYNC Pulsar or a different tool instead

evals.prompt: Reduce the motion blur on my monitor.
evals.expected_output: Motion blur is reduced by G-SYNC Pulsar, a separate tool from G-SYNC. The agent should select gassist_set_gsync_pulsar (enabled true) on a compatible monitor, or report it is unavailable if the display does not support it - not fall back to plain G-SYNC.
assertions: Read g-assist-mcp-skill/SKILL.md
Selected the G-SYNC Pulsar tool (gassist_set_gsync_pulsar) rather than plain G-SYNC
Called it to enable Pulsar, or reported it is unavailable on this display
Did not silently substitute gassist_set_display_gsync

evals.prompt: Make my monitor adjust its brightness to the room automatically.
evals.expected_output: Automatic, ambient-light brightness is Adaptive Brightness - a different tool from a fixed brightness percentage. The agent should select gassist_set_adaptive_brightness to enable it, rather than gassist_set_display_brightness.
assertions: Read g-assist-mcp-skill/SKILL.md
Selected gassist_set_adaptive_brightness rather than the fixed-percentage brightness tool
Enabled adaptive brightness, or reported it is unavailable on this display
Did not set a fixed brightness percentage instead

evals.prompt: Make my GPU as power-efficient as possible but keep at least 60 FPS.
evals.expected_output: This is the max performance-per-watt mode with a target FPS, not a plain frame-rate limit. The agent should select gassist_maxppw and enable it with the 60 FPS target taken from its enum, not gassist_frl.
assertions: Read g-assist-mcp-skill/SKILL.md
Selected gassist_maxppw rather than the frame-rate limiter
Enabled the mode with fps 60 taken from the tool's allowed values
Did not use gassist_frl to cap the frame rate instead

evals.prompt: Switch my monitor to esports mode.
evals.expected_output: gassist_set_monitor_preset switches the monitor image preset between DEFAULT and ESPORTS on supported monitors. The agent should call it with preset ESPORTS, or report it is unavailable if the monitor does not support presets.
assertions: Read g-assist-mcp-skill/SKILL.md
Called gassist_set_monitor_preset with preset ESPORTS
Took the preset value from the tool's enum
Reported unavailable rather than inventing a preset if the monitor lacks support

evals.prompt: Set my monitor brightness to 40%.
evals.expected_output: A fixed brightness level via gassist_set_display_brightness with percentage 40 (external monitors only; not laptop panels). The agent should call it once and report the result.
assertions: Read g-assist-mcp-skill/SKILL.md
Called gassist_set_display_brightness with percentage 40
Did not use adaptive brightness for a fixed value
Reported the outcome, or that it is unsupported on a laptop panel

evals.prompt: Reset my monitor's colours back to default.
evals.expected_output: gassist_restore_display_default_settings resets the requested settings; it is a change, so confirmation is collected by the host. The agent should call it with COLOR in the settings list and let the host confirm, not add a confirm argument or reset unrelated settings.
assertions: Read g-assist-mcp-skill/SKILL.md
Called gassist_restore_display_default_settings with COLOR in the settings list
Let the host collect confirmation rather than supplying one
Did not reset unrelated settings such as brightness or gamma

evals.prompt: What can G-Assist do on this machine?
evals.expected_output: A read-only overview from gassist_help describing the capabilities actually available on this machine. The agent should call the help tool and change nothing.
assertions: Read g-assist-mcp-skill/SKILL.md
Called gassist_help
Changed no settings
Summarised the capabilities from the tool result rather than from memory

evals.prompt: Set my monitor contrast to 75.

Called gassist_set_display_contrast with contrast 75 as an integer
Did not treat contrast as a percentage or a fixed enum
Reported the outcome, or that it is unsupported on a laptop panel

Called gassist_set_display_gamma with gamma "2.2" as a string, not a float
Took the value from the tool's enum
Reported the outcome

evals.expected_output: 2.1 is not one of the allowed gamma levels (1.2, 1.4, 1.6, 1.8, 2.0, 2.2, 2.4, 2.6). The agent should not force a non-enum value; it should offer the nearest allowed level (2.0 or 2.2) or ask the user to choose.

evals.prompt: Set my colour temperature to 6000K.

Called gassist_set_display_color_balance with all six axes (red, yellow, green, cyan, blue, magenta)

Called gassist_set_display_rgb_gain with percentage 90
Used the global percentage form, not per-channel

Called gassist_set_display_rgb_gain with red 80, green 75, and blue 70
